headline: Approved $2,740 for pedestrian buttons and plaque wording for White Cane Awareness Day, tabled PlanBTV wishlist discussion.
summary: The committee approved $2,740 in BACA funds for DPW to install new pedestrian buttons at Riverside Ave. and Hillside Terr. It also approved the wording for a plaque honoring Anne Connelly for White Cane Awareness Day, with one word change. The committee tabled further discussion of the PlanBTV 2050 wishlist until the next meeting and heard updates on playground renovations and a UVM Smart Apartment tour.
decisions: Approved allocating $2,740 from BACA funds to DPW for new pedestrian buttons at the Riverside Ave. and Hillside Terr. intersection.
Approved the White Cane Awareness Day plaque language, with "transformative" changed to "life-changing."
Tabled further discussion of the PlanBTV 2050 Wishlist until the next meeting.

Advisory Committee on Accessibility 
 
 
Monday, September 21, 2026, 3:00 PM, 3:00 pm, Sharon Bushor Conference Room, 
149 Church Street, OR Remotely via ZOOM 
 
 
Please click the link below to join the webinar: 
https://zoom.us/j/96458163787?pwd=cy0Oo4cojlRpMP3XzAx4UkLjx6FjMg.1 
Meeting ID: 964 5816 3787 
Passcode: 240456 
 
In Attendance: 
Nate Besio, Chair (NB) 
Lisa Black (LB) 
Meaghan Diffenderfer (MD) 
Karen Downey (KD) 
Sharon Henault (SH) 
Jacquie Kelley (JK) 
Ashley Parker (AP) 
 
Others in Attendance:  
Dan Norris, VABVI (DN) 
Scott Phillips, DPW (SP) 
Jackie Esperti, DPW (JE) 
Sophie Sauve, BPRW (SS) 
Bruce Wilson, Ward 8 Resident (BW) 
Hannah, Burlington Resident (H) 
 
Meeting called to order, 3:01 pm 
 
1. Adopt the Agenda 
SH moves to adopt the agenda  
MD seconds
All in favor, so moved and adopted 
 
2. Adopt Minutes 
KB Moves to adopt the minutes from the July meeting  
SH Seconds  
All in favor, so moved and approved 
 
3. Introductions 
 
Committee members introduce themselves.  
 
4. Public Forum 
 
Visitors DN, SP, JE, and SS introduce themselves.  
 
5. Committee News & Updates 
 
KD shares that there’s an event coming up with the Occupational Therapy 
department at UVM to take a tour of their Smart Apartment. Information will 
be shared with Nate so that the committee can join if available. This 
apartment is designed to showcase existing tools to help those with mobility 
& sensory challenges. The tour will be before Thanksgiving this year.  
 
6. DPW Funding Request 
 
JE and SP, on behalf of DPW, requests the use of the BACA Appropriated 
Funds of up to $2,740 for the instillation of new, updated pedestrian buttons 
at the intersection of Riverside Ave. and Hillside Terr.  
 
The committee provided feedback, including SH sharing challenges around 
use many existing pedestrian buttons in town. 
 
The DPW Team provided information on where the new wave pedestrian 
buttons have been installed, and potential solutions for current buttons that 
are not currently accessible for all users. 
 
DN proposes creating an informational video with DPW/VABVI around the 
new buttons, how to use them, and where they exist in the city.
KD moves to allocate $2,740 from the BACA Allocated Funding to DPW for 
pedestrian buttons for the Riverside and Hillside intersection. 
SH second the motion.  
All in favor, so moved and accepted.  
 
7. BPRW Playground Renovation 
 
SS provided a brief update from BPRW around several planned playground 
replacements in the coming years.  The meetings will be: September 24 
from 3-4 pm at Baird Park; October 1 from 3-4 pm at Ethan Alley Park; 
October 8 from 3-6 pm at Smalley Park. The BPRW team will get feedback 
from playground users, and notes that there will be a future invitation for a 
playground committee that will be assembled. 
 
Committee members ask clarifying questions and provide feedback on other 
parks to consider.  
 
8. White Cane Awareness Day 
 
DN explains the history of White Cane Awareness Day, and invites the 
committee to join on Oct. 16 at 10 am at 200 Pearl St. for the 62nd White 
Cane Awareness Day. The event will directly mirror the commute of Anne 
Connelly, the first Vermonter to have a white cane and guide dog, who 
travelled independently from Pearl St. to her office in City Hall. At the 
culmination of the event, a plaque will be dedicated and a proclamation read 
by the Mayor’s Office. DN asks the committee to approve the plaque 
language, which will then be purchased by VABVI. The plaque will read in 
print and braille: 
 
A professional blind woman who pioneered Services for the blind 
 
Here in 1928, Anne Connelly, Vermont Association for the Blind and 
Visually Impaired’s first teacher, taught students, and volunteers, to 
read, write and transcribe Braille. In 1929, she established a classroom 
to teach transformative life-changing independent living skills to blind 
Vermonters. Anne positively impacted public views on blindness as a 
professional, and by example, being the first blind Vermonter to travel 
with a white cane and with the first guide dog in Vermont, Betty.
Committee members provide feedback and reflection. SH suggests 
rewording “transformative”; committee elects “life-changing” in place.  
 
MD moves to approve the plague with the edit 
LB seconds  
All in favor, so moved and approved.  
 
9. PlanBTV 2050 Wishlist Discussion 
 
Since the wishlist has been distributed via email for committee review 
previously, MD will send to PlanBTV team, and the committee will table any 
larger discussions for the next meeting.  
 
SH would like to see a “Compliance and Review” Committee of sorts to 
ensure projects, especially with accessibility components, are being looked 
at with an accessibility lens and evaluated after completion to be sure the 
project is completed in full as contracted. This idea will be added to the list 
before a final copy is sent to the planBTV team.  
 
10. Other Committee Business 
 
MD reminds committee members that there is an available stipend. Details 
will be sent via email as well. 
 
SH shares that the City negotiated with Farrell on the Cambrian Way 
project, and part of that was to have an accessible path to the bike path. 
SH is looking to find who at the City should be contacted about to see the 
contract is adhered to.  
 
LB notes DRB would have approved this contract, and recommends 
reaching out to Permitting & Inspections.  
 
 
10. Adjournment 
 
Meeting adjourned: 4:05 pm.
